verdict.rationale: Obsidian documents two first-party programmatic surfaces. The Obsidian URI protocol lets external callers trigger actions such as opening or creating notes, and the public TypeScript plugin API (obsidian-api, including the Vault interface) exposes files and folders to code running inside the app. However, the evidence shows no external, general-purpose API (REST or local server) that an agent could use to drive the app broadly, and the URI actions shown are limited. Headless Sync is a sync client, not an API for driving the app, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: an external programmatic API beyond limited URI actions, a documented catalog of URI actions or API depth, and independent hands-on corroboration of agents driving Obsidian via these interfaces.
